title: Development
text: For changes to JAXCMR itself, use the optional repository checkout described in Local setup with VS Code. Run these commands from the repository root.

title: Development
text:
Prepare the environment
uv sync --locked --extra test --group reader
This installs the editable library, development tools, and notebook-test dependencies in one environment. The test extra adds only pytest. The default dev group includes the build and notebook tools for optional local checks; library CI does not install that group. Optional groups remain available: --group embeddings for sentence-transformers, --group profiling for line-profiler, and --extra experimental for the experimental Numba helper.

title: Development
text:
Edit and check notebooks
Edit original notebooks in templates/ or guide/, preserving useful saved outputs. Their short installation cells run only in Colab. Local and Slurm kernels use the environment the reader selected.
While changing executable code, run the affected cases:
uv run --no-sync python guide/tools/check_notebooks.py --select cat_recall_rate
Run all 17 cases before publishing changes to shared setup, example inputs, or library functionality:
uv run --no-sync python guide/tools/check_notebooks.py
The runner uses nbmake and pytest with two workers in the current environment. It executes temporary notebook copies, reduces workloads for testing, and reopens saved results in a separate process. The spreadsheet case uses synthetic inputs. Original notebook parameters and outputs are never rewritten. --jobs 1 runs serially; --platform windows selects the representative Windows cases. The report identifies the environment used and separates preparation and execution time.
Notebook execution is a local maintainer tool; GitHub Actions does not run notebooks or tests that execute notebook cells.
For prose and saved-output changes, render and check the website; execution is needed when calculations change. Adding a published notebook also requires adding its bounded case to the notebook test runner.

title: Development
text:
Test the library and installation
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests -m "not audit" \
  --ignore=tests/test_distribution.py \
  --ignore=tests/test_reader_checks.py \
  --ignore=tests/test_template_adaptation.py \
  --ignore=tests/test_documentation.py
While editing, select the relevant test file instead of repeating the full suite. Routine checks include scientific calculations, public validation, and complete modeling workflows. Three additional audit cases check compilation reuse in prepared losses and the gradient and evolutionary fitters:
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests -m audit
Run these checks before releases and when changing loss preparation or fitting compilation. Unfiltered pytest still includes the audit, notebook-related and distribution tests. Routine CI runs only the library selection above, against a normal installation made with python -m pip install ".[test]". It uses python -P -m pytest so Python does not import the adjacent checkout in place of the installed package. This tests dependency resolution from the package requirements; local editable development still uses uv.lock.
The optional local distribution tests build a wheel and source archive, rebuild from the archive, and install into a clean environment outside the checkout. They check the installed README example and offline preparation of all bundled inputs. Library tests cover input conflicts and custom paths; notebook checks exercise the current published notebooks. This separate installation check needs internet access for dependencies and does not run in CI:
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/test_distribution.py
New tests should catch incorrect behavior using independently established numerical answers or supported workflows. Put short derivations beside analytic expectations; identify historical regression values as such. Check observable results rather than private object identities, and use small doubles only at necessary boundaries. Required checks must not silently skip because private data is unavailable. When an assertion’s strength is uncertain, temporarily introduce the suspected fault and confirm that it fails for the intended reason. Keep the behavioral assertion, without adding a permanent test that reruns another test. Test our notebook preparation and result validation directly; rely on nbmake and pytest for notebook execution and failure reporting.
See the test fixtures and CI workflow.

title: Development
text:
Keep validation proportionate
Check inexpensive structural requirements where data enter an operation, especially when broadcasting or indexing could silently change observation or participant assignments. Keep value-dependent checks outside compiled calculations. Numerical analysis functions remain JIT-compatible and require valid inputs; full distance preflight checking remains optional. Test demonstrated failures through public operations without duplicating every check across wrappers and kernels.

title: Development
text:
Maintain the supplied examples
The eleven selected files under data/ and their fit methods document are the authoritative inputs. Packaging explicitly includes them; other research data and results remain excluded. The library’s fetch_inputs(paths, base_dir=...) copies only requested bundled examples, reuses matching files, and preserves conflicts and custom paths. An explicit revision= downloads reference bytes from GitHub on each call, including when checking an existing file. The default bundled route works offline. Neither route requires maintaining content hashes.
When changing a supplied input, update its methods or source notes as needed. The filenames are listed in jaxcmr/examples.py; adding an example also requires including it in the package configuration. jaxcmr.examples.fetch_inputs is the current import; jaxcmr.colab.fetch_inputs remains compatible with older notebooks. Reinstall the editable package to refresh its bundled resources, then run the notebook and distribution checks:
uv sync --locked --extra test --group reader --reinstall-package jaxcmr
The website stages downloads from those same authoritative files. Notebook explanation and analysis changes can be published without a package release. Library and bundled data changes require readers to update their installation; the Git installation route does not require a PyPI release.

title: Development
text:
Saved settings and older notebooks
Fit and simulation records describe the models, parameters, input paths, selected rows and run settings. Reuse checks compare these settings; fitting also recalculates the saved objective. Changes to data or code at an existing location require rerunning the affected calculations. Keep the input files and notebook with results you intend to reproduce.
Automatic source capture has been removed. Update older notebook copies that import capture_notebook or file_sha256 from jaxcmr.provenance; those functions and the provenance_dir, provenance_source_paths and notebook_source controls are no longer used. Existing records can retain obsolete digest fields, which no longer govern reuse.

title: Development
text:
Build and preview the website
Use Quarto 1.11.9, available on your command path, matching CI:
bash build-docs.sh
uv run --no-sync python guide/tools/check_site.py docs
uv run --no-sync python -m http.server 8786 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory docs
Open http://127.0.0.1:8786/. The build stages notebook pages and byte-for-byte source downloads before rendering, without executing notebooks. It removes retired generated files and protects source directories. Do not edit guide/templates/, guide/downloads/, or rendered HTML. Rebuild after edits; the file server serves the rebuilt pages.
Colab links and installation commands follow main. A local preview’s download includes local changes; its Colab button still opens the last pushed notebook.

title: Development
text:
Publication and release handover
The routine Checks and website workflow runs on pull requests targeting main, pushes to main, and manual requests. It has four testing/build jobs:

Library tests (Linux, macOS and Windows): one shared job definition runs separately on all three platforms, using Python 3.12 and CPU execution. Each installs JAXCMR normally with pip install ".[test]", then runs the same library tests and exclusions. A failure on one platform does not cancel the other platform runs.
Website: a Quarto build, download/link checks, and a downloadable preview artifact.

Feature-branch pushes do not also trigger a second run for an open pull request. Open a draft pull request to get automatic checks while working on a branch. There is no file-based change selection; each routine run performs the four jobs.
CI does not execute notebooks, test notebook cells or run the separate distribution rehearsal. The website build renders saved outputs and verifies download copies and links without executing notebooks. There is no additional platform-compatibility workflow. Notebook and distribution tools remain available for local use.
After the one-time Pages handover below, pushing documentation sources to main builds and publishes the website automatically. Local rendering remains useful for previewing changes; publishing no longer depends on committing generated HTML. Pull requests produce downloadable previews without publishing them.
Deployment waits for the Linux, macOS, Windows and website jobs to pass, then publishes the website artifact from that same run. It also checks that its commit is still the latest main. A manual workflow run can publish main through the same checks. No additional repository variable is required.
For the one-time handover:

Push the reviewed workflow and its supporting source changes. In repository Settings → Pages → Build and deployment, change Source from Deploy from a branch to GitHub Actions.
Run or rerun Checks and website for the current main commit, and verify that the library, website and deployment jobs all succeed. If branch rules require the previous job names, update those required checks when adopting this workflow.
Verify the public Setup pages, notebook downloads, example inputs, and Colab links. Check changed notebooks in hosted Colab separately, including a fresh runtime and your own input/output files.
After the replacement deployment is verified, remove docs/ from Git tracking and add /docs/ to .gitignore, keeping local rendered files available for previews.

Until the handover is completed, retain the tracked docs/ site and the existing branch-based publishing configuration. If the replacement deployment fails, the previous public site remains available; fix the failure and rerun the workflow.
PyPI publication remains separate. Before publishing a release, review the library and website checks, run the compilation audits, and select any additional local notebook or distribution checks needed for the changes being released. After publication, verify installation from PyPI in a clean environment before changing the short installation commands. A PyPI release is not required for ordinary notebook improvements or Git-based distribution.

title: Serial position curves
text:
Use a serial position curve to ask how recall varies with an item’s position in the study list. This procedure reads observed or simulated responses, calculates participant summaries for your selected conditions, and saves the comparison figure.
Early or late advantages describe a pattern that models may need to explain. The curve alone does not identify the mechanism producing that pattern.
For input conventions, see the data guide.

title: Serial position curves
text:
Configure this run
Choose response files, condition queries and an output folder. The default complete_lists_only=True restricts curves to lists with no padded study slots. For repeated study identities, size must accommodate the maximum number of positions occupied by one item.
Keep all editable settings in this tagged cell. Later cells derive paths and selections after any Papermill overrides.


1 — Set the parameters for this run
# Inputs and saved results — change these for your project.
project_root = None  # Explicit folder, enclosing Git root, or current directory.
data_path = None  # A supplied single path takes precedence over data_paths.
data_paths = [
    "data/Dupertuys2026.h5",
    "data/simulations/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo_best_of_3.h5",
    "data/simulations/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_source_only_demo_best_of_3.h5",
    "data/simulations/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_broad_demo_best_of_3.h5",
]
data_labels = ["Observed", "CMR", "Source-only eCMR", "Broader eCMR"]
output_dir = "results/spc"

# Observation selection — queries use fields in your dataset.
trial_query = None  # When supplied, use this one selection instead of trial_queries.
trial_queries = [
    "jnp.equal(data['list_type'], 1)",
    "jnp.equal(data['list_type'], 2)",
    "jnp.equal(data['list_type'], 3)",
]
labels = ["Mixed", "Pure emotional", "Pure neutral"]
selection_label = "Selected lists"
max_subjects = 0  # Zero keeps all participants; a positive value selects the first IDs.
complete_lists_only = True

# Scientific settings — choose these for the question you are asking.
size = 3  # Maximum study positions occupied by one item.

# Uncertainty and optional behavioral summaries.
confidence_level = 0.95
plot_seed = 0  # NumPy seed for bootstrap displays.

# Output overrides and appearance — None uses the default location or style.
figure_dir = None
figure_str = "spc"  # Empty displays the figure without saving it.
contrast_name = None  # Legend title for the selected comparisons.
color_cycle = None
ylim = None
yticks = None

title: Serial position curves
text:
Prepare the environment and inputs
Run the following setup cells once, then continue in order. The short installation cell runs only in Colab; local and Slurm runs use the environment you selected during Setup.
project_root anchors relative paths. When it is unset, Colab uses the current directory; elsewhere the notebook uses the enclosing Git project if present, or the current directory. Check the printed location. fetch_inputs copies requested bundled examples there, reuses matching files, and refuses to overwrite conflicting files. Custom input paths remain your responsibility.


2 — Prepare the Colab environment
import sys

if "google.colab" in sys.modules:
    %pip install --upgrade "jaxcmr @ git+https://github.com/githubpsyche/jaxcmr.git@main"




3 — Import packages
import jax.numpy as jnp
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from jaxcmr.analyses.spc import plot_spc
from jaxcmr.helpers import resolve_project_root, resolve_project_path, generate_trial_mask, load_data, save_figure

from jaxcmr.examples import fetch_inputs
from jaxcmr.dataset import select_conditions
from jaxcmr.plotting import comparison_panels

title: Serial position curves
text:
Select the observations
select_conditions returns the masks and participant coverage without altering your data. Check the printed list and participant counts before interpreting the results. Queries are Python expressions evaluated with the dataset named data; replace the supplied condition codes with those in your data. trial_query overrides the list of trial_queries and uses selection_label.
With data_path set, the notebook reads that file and compares conditions. With data_path=None, data_paths and data_labels produce one panel per condition comparing datasets—even if the list contains just one file. Labels must correspond to the supplied selections and files.


4 — Resolve input paths, conditions and output settings
root_path = resolve_project_root(project_root)
print("Project directory:", root_path)

fetch_inputs([data_path] if data_path is not None else data_paths, base_dir=root_path)

np.random.seed(plot_seed)
output_dir = resolve_project_path(output_dir, root_path)
figure_dir = resolve_project_path(figure_dir, root_path) if figure_dir is not None else output_dir

queries = trial_queries if trial_query is None else [trial_query]
condition_labels = labels if trial_query is None else [selection_label]
input_paths = [data_path] if data_path is not None else data_paths
input_paths = [resolve_project_path(path, root_path) for path in input_paths]
input_labels = [selection_label] if data_path is not None else data_labels
if len(queries) != len(condition_labels) or len(input_paths) != len(input_labels):
    raise ValueError("Supply a label for each input and each condition query.")




5 — Load the supplied response datasets
datasets = [load_data(str(path), max_subjects=max_subjects) for path in input_paths]




6 — Select observations and report participant counts
selected_conditions = [
    select_conditions(dataset, queries, complete_lists_only=complete_lists_only)
    for dataset in datasets
]
masks_by_dataset = [[condition.mask for condition in group] for group in selected_conditions]
for dataset_label, group in zip(input_labels, selected_conditions):
    for condition_label, condition in zip(condition_labels, group):
        print(
            f"{dataset_label} / {condition_label}: {condition.trial_count} lists, "
            f"{condition.participant_count} participants"
        )
data, trial_masks = datasets[0], masks_by_dataset[0]

CMR / Pure emotional: 1220 lists, 122 participants

Source-only eCMR / Pure emotional: 1220 lists, 122 participants
Source-only eCMR / Pure neutral: 1230 lists, 123 participants

Broader eCMR / Pure emotional: 1220 lists, 122 participants

title: Serial position curves
text:
Calculate and interpret the curves
The analysis calculates recall by study position within each participant, then displays participant means and bootstrap confidence intervals. For repeated study identities, recall is credited to the item’s presentation positions using the configured capacity.
Compare the shape and magnitude of curves under matched observation selections. Confidence intervals describe uncertainty across participants; they do not by themselves test a difference between curves. Use separate statistical comparisons for a specific hypothesis.


7 — Prepare the condition and dataset comparison panels
panels = comparison_panels(
    datasets, masks_by_dataset, input_labels, condition_labels,
    mode="conditions" if data_path is not None else "datasets",
    selection_label=selection_label,
)




8 — Calculate, plot and save the selected comparison
fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(panels), 1, figsize=(8, 3.8 * len(panels)), squeeze=False)
for ax, panel in zip(axes.ravel(), panels):
    panel_data = panel["datasets"]
    panel_masks = panel["trial_masks"]
    curve_labels = panel["labels"]
    title = panel["title"]
    plot_spc(
        panel_data,
        panel_masks,
        size=size,
        labels=curve_labels,
        contrast_name=contrast_name,
        color_cycle=color_cycle,
        confidence_level=confidence_level,
        axis=ax,
    )
    ax.set_title(title)

    if ax.get_legend_handles_labels()[1]:
        ax.legend(title=contrast_name)
    if ylim is not None:
        ax.set_ylim(ylim)
    if yticks is not None:
        ax.set_yticks(yticks)
save_figure(str(figure_dir), figure_str)

title: Serial position curves
text:
Reuse the results
The figure is saved to figure_dir or, when unset, output_dir, using figure_str as its name. Set a distinct output folder for another selection. The input response files remain unchanged and can also be used for output-position or transition analyses.
The Templates overview describes how saved products connect.

title: Recall by output position
text:
Use this procedure to ask which study positions supply the first, third, or another response in a recall sequence. It reads observed or simulated responses and saves curves for the output positions and conditions you select.
Study position describes where an item appeared during presentation; output position describes when it was recalled. This distinction matters when configuring and interpreting later-recall curves.
For input conventions, see the data guide.

title: Recall by output position
text:
Configure this run
Choose response files and conditions, then set output_positions. These are zero-based: [0, 2] means the first and third response. The optional query_recall_position overrides that list with a single position. Requested positions must fit within the stored recall array.
The default selects complete study lists. size controls the capacity for repeated study identities, as in the serial-position analysis.
Keep all editable settings in this tagged cell. Later cells derive paths and selections after any Papermill overrides.


1 — Set the parameters for this run
# Inputs and saved results — change these for your project.
project_root = None  # Explicit folder, enclosing Git root, or current directory.
data_path = None  # A supplied single path takes precedence over data_paths.
data_paths = [
    "data/Dupertuys2026.h5",
    "data/simulations/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo_best_of_3.h5",
    "data/simulations/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_source_only_demo_best_of_3.h5",
    "data/simulations/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_broad_demo_best_of_3.h5",
]
data_labels = ["Observed", "CMR", "Source-only eCMR", "Broader eCMR"]
output_dir = "results/pnr"

# Observation selection — queries use fields in your dataset.
trial_query = None  # When supplied, use this one selection instead of trial_queries.
trial_queries = [
    "jnp.equal(data['list_type'], 1)",
    "jnp.equal(data['list_type'], 2)",
    "jnp.equal(data['list_type'], 3)",
]
labels = ["Mixed", "Pure emotional", "Pure neutral"]
selection_label = "Selected lists"
max_subjects = 0  # Zero keeps all participants; a positive value selects the first IDs.
complete_lists_only = True

# Scientific settings — choose these for the question you are asking.
output_positions = [0, 2]  # Zero-based: first and third response.
size = 3  # Maximum study positions occupied by one item.

# Uncertainty and optional behavioral summaries.
confidence_level = 0.95
plot_seed = 0  # NumPy seed for bootstrap displays.

# Output overrides and appearance — None uses the default location or style.
figure_dir = None
figure_str = "pnr"  # Empty displays the figure without saving it.
contrast_name = None  # Legend title for the selected comparisons.
color_cycle = None
ylim = None
yticks = None

# Optional input overrides and compatibility names.
query_recall_position = None  # Optional single position, zero-based.

title: Recall by output position
text:
Interpret the output-position curves
The plot divides actual choices at each study position by opportunities where that item remains available at the selected output position, within participant. At the first output this describes first-recall probability; later outputs condition on availability after prior recalls. Later curves need not sum to one across study positions.
A zero-padded missing response contributes no actual choice. The calculation is not restricted to sequences that produced a response at that output position. The figure then averages participant curves and shows participant-bootstrap intervals.


7 — Prepare the condition and dataset comparison panels
panels = comparison_panels(
    datasets, masks_by_dataset, input_labels, condition_labels,
    mode="conditions" if data_path is not None else "datasets",
    selection_label=selection_label,
)

positions = (
    [query_recall_position] if query_recall_position is not None else output_positions
)
position_panels = []
for panel in panels:
    for position in positions:
        position_panels.append({**panel, "position": position})
panels = position_panels




8 — Calculate, plot and save the selected comparison
fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(panels), 1, figsize=(8, 3.8 * len(panels)), squeeze=False)
for ax, panel in zip(axes.ravel(), panels):
    panel_data = panel["datasets"]
    panel_masks = panel["trial_masks"]
    curve_labels = panel["labels"]
    title = panel["title"]
    position = panel["position"]
    plot_pnr(
        panel_data,
        panel_masks,
        size=size,
        query_recall_position=position,
        labels=curve_labels,
        contrast_name=contrast_name,
        color_cycle=color_cycle,
        confidence_level=confidence_level,
        axis=ax,
    )
    title += f" — response {position + 1}"
    ax.set_title(title)

    if ax.get_legend_handles_labels()[1]:
        ax.legend(title=contrast_name)
    if ylim is not None:
        ax.set_ylim(ylim)
    if yticks is not None:
        ax.set_yticks(yticks)
save_figure(str(figure_dir), figure_str)

text:
Reuse the results
The saved figure contains the requested output-position comparisons. figure_dir overrides output_dir; figure_str sets the filename. To study another response, change output_positions (and clear query_recall_position if using the list) before rerunning.

title: Comparing pooled model fits
text:
Use this procedure to compare saved pooled model fits and their saved predictions. It checks the observations and objective conventions, recalculates likelihoods, and saves a model-comparison table alongside optimization histories and behavioral figures.
You need at least two compatible pooled fit records, their response files and response provenance. Fitting and simulation are separate procedures. The results here concern parameter sets fitted across participants; they are not a comparison of independent participant estimates.
For input conventions, see the data guide.

title: Comparing pooled model fits
text:
Configure this run
Use matching model keys in fit_paths, simulation_paths and model_labels. Supply the same observations used for fitting. The shared fit selection is read from the records; the behavioral display selection is configured separately through analysis_trial_query or individual analysis configurations.
Choose output_dir for the comparison table and figures. The behavioral analysis list selects what to inspect; a better fit score does not guarantee better predictions for every behavioral measure.
Keep all editable settings in this tagged cell. Later cells derive paths and selections after any Papermill overrides.


1 — Configure the saved fits and response files
# Inputs and saved results — change these for your project.
project_root = None  # Explicit folder, enclosing Git root, or current directory.
data_path = "data/Dupertuys2026.h5"
output_dir = "results/model_comparison"

# Models and saved fits — names connect specifications, labels and outputs.
fit_paths = {
    "CMR": "data/fits/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo.json",
    "eCMR_source_only": "data/fits/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_source_only.json",
    "eCMR_broad": "data/fits/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_broad.json",
}
simulation_paths = {
    "CMR": "data/simulations/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo_best_of_3.h5",
    "eCMR_source_only": "data/simulations/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_source_only_demo_best_of_3.h5",
    "eCMR_broad": "data/simulations/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_broad_demo_best_of_3.h5",
}
model_labels = {
    "CMR": "CMR",
    "eCMR_source_only": "Source-only eCMR",
    "eCMR_broad": "Broader eCMR",
}

# Fitting and simulation — optimizer controls are separate from model parameters.

Feature composition stays explicit here. feature_column selects the categorical feature, and concat_features=True combines categorical columns before semantic columns. When concatenation is requested, supply both feature arrays; otherwise the configured concatenation fails rather than substituting a different feature set.


4 — Define feature loading and model construction
def load_features(spec):
    semantic = np.load(resolve_project_path(spec["embedding_path"], root_path)) if spec.get("embedding_path") else None
    categorical = (
        np.load(resolve_project_path(spec["emotion_feature_path"], root_path))[
            :,
            int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) : int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) + 1,
        ]
        if spec.get("emotion_feature_path")
        else None
    )
    if spec.get("concat_features", False):
        return np.concatenate([categorical, semantic], axis=1)
    return categorical if categorical is not None else semantic


def construct_model(spec):
    return import_from_string(spec["model_factory"])(
        **{name: import_from_string(path) for name, path in spec["components"].items()}
    )

section: Establish a comparable set of fits
text:
Establish a comparable set of fits
All records must contain one pooled fit and the same nonempty set of observation rows. The notebook also checks the recorded input path when available, objective and stopping policy. A matching path does not establish identical data: use the same observations for every fit, and refit after changing them. Models may differ in mechanisms and free parameters, but their likelihood scores must refer to comparable observations and conventions.


6 — Load the named pooled fits
records = {name: json.loads(resolve_project_path(path, root_path).read_text()) for name, path in fit_paths.items()}
display_labels = {name: model_labels.get(name, name) for name in records}




7 — Establish matching observations, objectives and stopping rules
first = next(iter(records.values()))
selected_rows = sorted(first["selected_trial_indices"])
if (
    len(records) < 2
    or not selected_rows
    or len(set(selected_rows)) != len(selected_rows)
):
    raise ValueError(
        "Compare at least two pooled fits with a nonempty observation selection."
    )
for name, record in records.items():
    if record["fits"]["subject"] != [-1] or len(record["fitness"]) != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} is not a single pooled fit.")
    if (
        record.get("data_path", data_source) != data_source
        or sorted(record["selected_trial_indices"]) != selected_rows
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: observations or selected rows differ.")
    if (
        record["loss_function"] != first["loss_function"]
        or record["components"]["termination_policy_create_fn"]
        != first["components"]["termination_policy_create_fn"]
    ):
        raise ValueError("These fits do not use a common objective and stopping rule.")
comparison_mask = (
    jnp.zeros(len(subjects), dtype=bool).at[jnp.asarray(selected_rows)].set(True)
)
print(len(selected_rows), "shared lists; objective:", first["loss_function"])
print("Stopping policy:", first["components"]["termination_policy_create_fn"])

title: Comparing pooled model fits
text:
Recalculate likelihoods
The notebook rebuilds each saved model and evaluates the recorded physical parameter values on the shared observations. This checks numerical consistency with the saved result. It does not rerun optimization or establish convergence to a global optimum.


9 — Check saved likelihoods against the current inputs
recalculated = {}
for name, record in records.items():
    model_factory = construct_model(record)
    features = load_features(record)
    loss_class = import_from_string(record["loss_function"])
    fixed = (
        record.get("fit_configuration", {})
        .get("parameters", {})
        .get("fixed", record["fixed"])
    )
    names = tuple(record["free"])
    evaluate = make_scipy_loss_fn(
        loss_class(model_factory, data, features),
        jnp.asarray(selected_rows),
        fixed,
        names,
    )
    values = jnp.asarray([record["fits"][key][0] for key in names])
    recalculated[name] = float(evaluate(values))
    if not np.isclose(recalculated[name], record["fitness"][0], rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-5):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{name}: saved NLL does not match the installed implementation and inputs."
        )
print(
    tabulate(
        [
            {
                "Model": display_labels[name],
                "Saved NLL": record["fitness"][0],
                "Recalculated NLL": recalculated[name],
            }
            for name, record in records.items()
        ],
        headers="keys",
        floatfmt=".6f",
    )
)

section: Compare fit scores and search histories
text:
Compare fit scores and search histories
The table reports negative log likelihood, the number of free parameters, AIC and differences from the smallest AIC. AIC adds a parameter-count penalty to the likelihood score; lower values are preferred within this eligible comparison.
Inspect optimization histories alongside the score table: a poorer result may reflect an unsuccessful search. These are pooled fits, so model-score differences are not participant-level paired observations.


10 — Calculate and save pooled AIC comparisons
from jaxcmr.summarize import calculate_aic

# The configured objectives must be unscaled negative log likelihoods.
comparison_records = [
    {**record, "name": name, "fitness": [recalculated[name]]}
    for name, record in records.items()
]
aic_scores = calculate_aic(comparison_records).set_index("Model")["AIC"]
comparison = [
    {
        "Model": display_labels[name],
        "Free parameters": len(record["free"]),
        "Negative log likelihood": recalculated[name],
        "AIC": float(aic_scores.loc[name]),
    }
    for name, record in records.items()
]
best = min(row["AIC"] for row in comparison)
for row in comparison:
    row["Delta AIC"] = row["AIC"] - best
print(tabulate(comparison, headers="keys", floatfmt=".3f"))
with (output_dir / "pooled_model_comparison.csv").open("w", newline="") as stream:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(stream, fieldnames=list(comparison[0]))
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(comparison)

text:
Compare saved predictions
The saved simulation settings are checked against the fitted models and simulation settings before plotting. Behavioral comparisons complement likelihood-based scores by showing where a model succeeds or fails.
The supplied responses were generated with observed recall lengths imposed. Their agreement in length is not a prediction of stopping. Repeated simulations retain the original participant IDs when computing summaries.


12 — Load the responses produced by the fitting or simulation procedure
simulations = {}
for name, record in records.items():
    path = resolve_project_path(simulation_paths[name], root_path)
    metadata = json.loads(path.with_suffix(".json").read_text())
    expected = {
        "data_path": data_source,
        "selected_trial_indices": selected_rows,
        "fits": record["fits"],
        "model_factory": record["model_factory"],
        "components": record["components"],
        "simulation_function": record["simulation_function"],
    }
    if any(metadata.get(key) != value for key, value in expected.items()):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{name}: saved responses belong to a different fit or observation selection."
        )
    simulated = load_data(str(path))
    if filter_repeated_recalls:
        simulated = dict(simulated)
        simulated["recalls"] = repetition.filter_repeated_recalls(simulated["recalls"])
    simulations[name] = simulated
    print(
        display_labels[name],
        "—",
        path,
        "— seed",
        metadata["seed"],
        "— repetitions",
        metadata["experiment_count"],
    )
figure_dir = resolve_project_path(figure_dir, root_path) if figure_dir is not None else output_dir
figure_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

comparison_groups = []
if redo_figures and simulations:
    observed = dict(data)
    if filter_repeated_recalls:
        observed["recalls"] = repetition.filter_repeated_recalls(observed["recalls"])
    datasets = [observed, *simulations.values()]
    names = ["Observed", *[display_labels[name] for name in simulations]]
    comparison_groups.append(
        {
            "analyses": comparison_analysis_configs,
            "datasets": datasets,
            "labels": names,
            "base_masks": [comparison_mask, *[None for _ in simulations]],
            "suffix": "",
        }
    )
    for dataset_index, (dataset, label) in enumerate(zip(datasets, names)):
        comparison_groups.append(
            {
                "analyses": single_analysis_configs,
                "datasets": [dataset],
                "labels": [label],
                "base_masks": [comparison_mask if dataset_index == 0 else None],
                "suffix": f"_single_{dataset_index}",
            }
        )

    analysis_configs = group["analyses"]

    for figure, figure_suffix in iter_analysis_figures(

title: Comparing pooled model fits
text:
Reuse the results
pooled_model_comparison.csv in output_dir records the model scores. Retain it with the search-history and behavioral figures and the original fits/responses. The table is evidence about the configured pooled comparison, not a general ranking of model families.
To extend the comparison, first fit and simulate the additional specification using compatible observations and objective conventions, then add matching entries to the path dictionaries.
The Templates overview describes how saved products connect.

title: Fitting models
text:
Use this procedure to estimate parameters for one or more specified models from your observations. It saves fit records that the simulation and model-comparison templates can read, and can also generate responses and behavioral figures.
A model specification describes the mechanism, fixed values and bounds for fitted parameters. Optimizer settings describe how the search is conducted. The defaults fit three related models to the supplied observations using one pooled parameter set per model. You can instead select one model, a subset of participants, or separate participant fits.
For input conventions, see the data guide.

title: Fitting models
text:
Configure this run
Start with data_path, output_dir, the observation selection and model_configs. For each model, inspect the component choices, parameters["fixed"], parameters["free"] and their bounds. A one-entry model_configs dictionary runs one model and is also a useful independent batch job.
pooled=True estimates one parameter set across the selected participants; pooled=False estimates participant-specific sets. subject_indices refers to positions in the sorted participant-ID list, not to the IDs themselves. Splitting a pooled fit into participant jobs changes the scientific analysis.
Set search effort in fit_hyperparams, separately from model parameters. The default optimizer settings can take substantial time. redo_fits=False reuses a compatible existing file, but still starts optimization if that file is absent. Set both redo_sims and redo_figures to False for a fit-only run. Use a distinct output folder or run tag for a new specification.
Keep all editable settings in this tagged cell. Later cells derive paths and selections after any Papermill overrides.

title: Fitting models
text:
Prepare the environment and inputs
Run the following setup cells once, then continue in order. The short installation cell runs only in Colab; local and Slurm runs use the environment you selected during Setup.
project_root anchors relative paths. When it is unset, Colab uses the current directory; elsewhere the notebook uses the enclosing Git project if present, or the current directory. Check the printed location. fetch_inputs copies requested bundled examples there, reuses matching files, and refuses to overwrite conflicting files. Custom input paths remain your responsibility.


2 — Prepare the Colab environment
import sys

if "google.colab" in sys.modules:
    %pip install --upgrade "jaxcmr @ git+https://github.com/githubpsyche/jaxcmr.git@main"




3 — Import packages
import json
from pathlib import Path

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from tabulate import tabulate

import jaxcmr
from jaxcmr import repetition
from jaxcmr.fitting import make_scipy_loss_fn, validate_fit_compatibility
from jaxcmr.helpers import (
    resolve_project_root,
    resolve_project_path,
    generate_trial_mask,
    import_from_string,
    load_data,
    save_dict_to_hdf5,
    save_figure,
)
from jaxcmr.simulation import simulate_h5_from_h5


from jaxcmr.examples import fetch_inputs
from jaxcmr.plotting import iter_analysis_figures
from jaxcmr.fitting import parameters_for_subjects
from jaxcmr.provenance import simulation_metadata_matches


Feature composition stays explicit here. feature_column selects the categorical feature, and concat_features=True combines categorical columns before semantic columns. When concatenation is requested, supply both feature arrays; otherwise the configured concatenation fails rather than substituting a different feature set.


4 — Define feature loading and model construction
def load_features(spec):
    semantic = np.load(resolve_project_path(spec["embedding_path"], root_path)) if spec.get("embedding_path") else None
    categorical = (
        np.load(resolve_project_path(spec["emotion_feature_path"], root_path))[
            :,
            int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) : int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) + 1,
        ]
        if spec.get("emotion_feature_path")
        else None
    )
    if spec.get("concat_features", False):
        return np.concatenate([categorical, semantic], axis=1)
    return categorical if categorical is not None else semantic


def construct_model(spec):
    return import_from_string(spec["model_factory"])(
        **{name: import_from_string(path) for name, path in spec["components"].items()}
    )




5 — Load observations and establish runtime settings
root_path = resolve_project_root(project_root)
print("Project directory:", root_path)

fetch_inputs([data_path], base_dir=root_path)

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", enable_x64)

data_source = (data_path.relative_to(root_path).as_posix()
               if data_path.is_relative_to(root_path) else str(data_path))
subjects = np.asarray(data["subject"]).ravel()

title: Fitting models
text:
Inspect the work unit
The next cells select observations, create output locations and report the participants, models and free-parameter counts. trial_query controls the fitting observations. analysis_trial_query later controls behavioral displays; it does not change the observations used to fit the model.
Check the printed selection before launching optimization. target_directory, fit_dir, simulation_dir and figure_dir override their respective default locations; changing output_dir alone does not redirect an explicit override.


8 — Select the participant work unit and observation trials
data_tag = data_tag or data_path.stem
subject_ids = np.unique(subjects)
if max_subjects:
    subject_ids = subject_ids[:max_subjects]
cohort_mask = generate_trial_mask(data, trial_query) & jnp.isin(
    data["subject"].ravel(), subject_ids
)
if subject_indices:
    subject_ids = subject_ids[np.asarray(subject_indices, dtype=int)]
comparison_mask = cohort_mask & jnp.isin(data["subject"].ravel(), subject_ids)
selected_rows = np.flatnonzero(np.asarray(comparison_mask)).tolist()
if not selected_rows:
    raise ValueError("The configured selection contains no observations.")
if not model_configs:
    raise ValueError("Supply at least one model configuration.")




9 — Prepare output directories
product_root = resolve_project_path(target_directory, root_path) if target_directory is not None else output_dir
fit_dir = resolve_project_path(fit_dir, root_path) if fit_dir is not None else product_root / "fits"

    resolve_project_path(simulation_dir, root_path) if simulation_dir is not None else product_root / "simulations"
)

    resolve_project_path(figure_dir, root_path) if figure_dir is not None else product_root / "figures/fitting"
)
for directory in [fit_dir, simulation_dir, figure_dir]:
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)




10 — Summarize the selected work unit and model settings
print(
    f"Selected {len(selected_rows)} lists from {len(np.unique(subjects[selected_rows]))} participants."
)
display_labels = {name: spec.get("label", name) for name, spec in model_configs.items()}
print(
    tabulate(
        [
            {
                "Model": display_labels[name],
                "Free parameters": len(spec["parameters"]["free"]),

            for name, spec in model_configs.items()
        ],

    )
)

11 — Prepare model-specific filenames and fit configurations
fit_paths, simulation_paths, selections, fit_configurations = {}, {}, {}, {}
fitter_class = import_from_string(fit_alg_path)
loss_class = import_from_string(loss_fn_path)
for model_name, model_spec in model_configs.items():
    parameter_config = model_spec["parameters"]
    features = load_features(model_spec)
    search_settings = {
        **fit_hyperparams,
        "seed": model_spec["seed"],
        "bounds": parameter_config["free"],
    }
    run_tag = f"{base_run_tag}_best_of_{search_settings.get('best_of', 1)}"
    if max_subjects:
        run_tag += f"_nsubs_{max_subjects}"
    model_run_stem = f"{data_tag}_{model_name}_{run_tag}"
    stem = model_spec.get("output_stem", model_run_stem)
    if subject_indices:
        stem += "_sub" + "_".join(str(index) for index in subject_indices)
    fit_path = fit_dir / f"{stem}.json"
    if fit_path in fit_paths.values():
        raise ValueError("Each model needs a distinct output_stem.")
    fit_paths[model_name] = fit_path
    simulation_paths[model_name] = simulation_dir / f"{stem}.h5"
    selections[model_name] = comparison_mask
    configuration = {
        "data_path": data_source,
        "selected_trial_indices": selected_rows,
        "cohort_trial_indices": np.flatnonzero(np.asarray(cohort_mask)).tolist(),
        "model_factory": model_spec["model_factory"],
        "components": model_spec["components"],
        "loss_function": loss_fn_path,
        "fit_algorithm": fit_alg_path,
        "parameters": parameter_config,
        "search_settings": search_settings,
        "pooled": pooled,
        "embedding_path": model_spec.get("embedding_path", ""),
        "emotion_feature_path": model_spec.get("emotion_feature_path", ""),
        "feature_column": model_spec.get("feature_column", 6),
        "concat_features": model_spec.get("concat_features", False),
        "jax_enable_x64": enable_x64,
    }

    for key in ("embedding_path", "emotion_feature_path"):
        if configuration[key]:
            feature_path = resolve_project_path(configuration[key], root_path)
            configuration[key] = (feature_path.relative_to(root_path).as_posix()
                          if feature_path.is_relative_to(root_path) else str(feature_path))
    fit_configurations[model_name] = configuration

title: Fitting models
text:
Fit or reuse saved results
Each model has a separate fit path and recorded configuration. Existing fits are checked against the requested model, observations, parameter bounds and search settings before reuse. Saved settings identify the requested run; they do not detect edits to files or code in place. After such edits, set redo_fits=True and regenerate affected simulations. Accepted older records still require objective recalculation. A compatibility check is not evidence that optimization found the best solution.
For every returned fit, the notebook independently recalculates the objective from the saved physical parameter values. A disagreement stops the run. In the supplied likelihood configuration, the objective is negative log likelihood, so smaller values are better. Inspect bounds and search behavior as well as the final value.


12 — Prepare metadata for newly fitted records
fit_metadata = {}
for model_name, model_spec in model_configs.items():
    configuration = fit_configurations[model_name]
    search_settings = configuration["search_settings"]
    stem = fit_paths[model_name].stem
    run_tag = f"{base_run_tag}_best_of_{search_settings.get('best_of', 1)}"
    if max_subjects:
        run_tag += f"_nsubs_{max_subjects}"
    fit_metadata[model_name] = {
        "name": stem,
        "model": model_name,
        "label": display_labels[model_name],
        "pooled": pooled,
        "data_tag": data_tag,
        "data_query": trial_query,
        "trial_query": trial_query,
        "run_tag": run_tag,
        "data_path": data_source,
        "selected_trial_indices": selected_rows,
        "cohort_trial_indices": configuration["cohort_trial_indices"],
        "model_factory": model_spec["model_factory"],
        "components": model_spec["components"],
        "loss_function": loss_fn_path,
        "fit_algorithm": fit_alg_path,
        "simulation_function": sim_alg_path,
        "fit_configuration": configuration,
        "jaxcmr_version": jaxcmr.__version__,
        "jax_version": jax.__version__,
        "jax_enable_x64": enable_x64,
        "embedding_path": configuration["embedding_path"],
        "emotion_feature_path": configuration["emotion_feature_path"],
        "feature_column": configuration["feature_column"],
        "concat_features": configuration["concat_features"],
        "simulation_seed": simulation_seed,
        "simulation_repetitions": experiment_count,
    }




13 — Fit or load, recalculate the objective and save each model
records = {}
fitted_now = set()
recalculated_objectives = {}
for model_name, model_spec in model_configs.items():
    parameter_config = model_spec["parameters"]
    model_factory = construct_model(model_spec)
    features = load_features(model_spec)
    configuration = fit_configurations[model_name]
    search_settings = configuration["search_settings"]
    fit_path = fit_paths[model_name]
    if redo_fits or not fit_path.exists():
        fitter = fitter_class(
            data,
            features,
            parameter_config["fixed"],
            model_factory,
            loss_class,
            hyperparams=search_settings,
        )
        actual_subjects = np.unique(subjects[selected_rows])
        if pooled:
            fit_record = fitter.fit(comparison_mask, subject_id=-1)
        elif len(actual_subjects) == 1:
            fit_record = fitter.fit(comparison_mask, subject_id=int(actual_subjects[0]))
        else:
            fit_record = fitter.fit_subjects(comparison_mask)
        fitted_now.add(model_name)
    else:
        fit_record = json.loads(fit_path.read_text())
        try:
            validate_fit_compatibility(fit_record, configuration)
        except ValueError as error:
            raise ValueError(f"{model_name}: {error}") from error
        # Complete accepted older metadata after checking it; do not rewrite the file.
        for key in ("model_factory", "components", "loss_function", "data_path"):
            fit_record.setdefault(key, configuration[key])
        fit_record.setdefault("simulation_function", sim_alg_path)
        fit_record.setdefault("fit_configuration", configuration)
        fit_record.setdefault("pooled", pooled)
    expected_subjects = [-1] if pooled else np.unique(subjects[selected_rows]).tolist()
    if sorted(fit_record["fits"]["subject"]) != expected_subjects:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{model_name}: fit rows do not match the selected participants."
        )

    # Evaluate the returned physical parameters independently of optimizer state.
    loss = loss_class(model_factory, data, features)
    free_parameter_names = tuple(parameter_config["free"])
    recalculated = []
    for subject_index, subject_id in enumerate(fit_record["fits"]["subject"]):
        subject_trials = (
            comparison_mask
            if pooled
            else comparison_mask & (data["subject"].ravel() == subject_id)
        )
        evaluate = make_scipy_loss_fn(
            loss,
            jnp.flatnonzero(subject_trials),
            parameter_config["fixed"],
            free_parameter_names,
        )
        free_parameter_values = jnp.asarray(
            [fit_record["fits"][key][subject_index] for key in free_parameter_names]
        )
        recalculated.append(float(evaluate(free_parameter_values)))
    if not np.allclose(fit_record["fitness"], recalculated, rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-5):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{model_name}: returned objective disagrees with recalculation."
        )
    if model_name in fitted_now:
        fit_record.update(fit_metadata[model_name])
        fit_record["recomputed_objective"] = recalculated
        if loss_fn_path.endswith("ExcludeTerminationLikelihoodLoss") and pooled:
            fit_record["recomputed_nll"] = recalculated[0]
        fit_path.write_text(json.dumps(fit_record, indent=2) + "\n")
    records[model_name] = fit_record
    recalculated_objectives[model_name] = recalculated




14 — Display fitted parameters and independently recalculated objectives
for model_name, fit_record in records.items():
    fit_path = fit_paths[model_name]
    free_parameter_names = tuple(model_configs[model_name]["parameters"]["free"])
    recalculated = recalculated_objectives[model_name]
    print(display_labels[model_name], "—", fit_path)
    print(
        tabulate(
            {
                key: fit_record["fits"][key]
                for key in ["subject", *free_parameter_names]
            },
            headers="keys",
            floatfmt=".5g",
        )
    )
    print(
        tabulate(
            zip(fit_record["fits"]["subject"], fit_record["fitness"], recalculated),
            headers=["Subject", "Reported objective", "Recalculated"],
            floatfmt=".6f",
        )
    )
print("fit_paths =", {model_name: str(path) for model_name, path in fit_paths.items()})

title: Fitting models
text:
Generate responses when requested
This stage runs when simulations or behavioral figures are requested. parameters_for_subjects assigns the parameter rows by participant identity. A pooled parameter set is assigned to every selected participant; participant fits retain their assignments. experiment_count repeats each selected experiment, and simulation_seed controls sampling. Repetitions remain grouped under their original participant IDs.
The default simulator forces the observed recall counts. It can test predicted item choices and organization under those lengths, but matching lengths are imposed rather than predicted. Matching saved responses can be reused when redo_sims=False; a newly fitted model or incompatible response provenance requires fresh responses.


15 — Prepare participant parameters and simulation settings
simulation_inputs = {}
for model_name, fit_record in records.items():
    if not (redo_sims or redo_figures):
        continue
    model_factory = construct_model(fit_record)
    features = load_features(fit_record)
    selected_trials = selections[model_name]
    is_pooled = fit_record.get("pooled", fit_record["fits"]["subject"] == [-1])
    participant_ids = jnp.unique(data["subject"].ravel()[selected_trials])
    subject_parameters = parameters_for_subjects(fit_record, participant_ids)
    configuration = {
        "fits": fit_record["fits"],
        "pooled": is_pooled,
        "jax_enable_x64": enable_x64,
        "jaxcmr_version": jaxcmr.__version__,
        "model_factory": fit_record["model_factory"],
        "components": fit_record["components"],
        "simulation_function": fit_record["simulation_function"],
        "data_path": data_source,
        "selected_trial_indices": np.flatnonzero(np.asarray(selected_trials)).tolist(),
        "embedding_path": fit_record.get("embedding_path", ""),
        "emotion_feature_path": fit_record.get("emotion_feature_path", ""),
        "feature_column": fit_record.get("feature_column", 6),
        "concat_features": fit_record.get("concat_features", False),
        "seed": simulation_seed,
        "experiment_count": experiment_count,
    }

    for key in ("embedding_path", "emotion_feature_path"):
        if configuration[key]:
            feature_path = resolve_project_path(configuration[key], root_path)
            configuration[key] = (feature_path.relative_to(root_path).as_posix()
                          if feature_path.is_relative_to(root_path) else str(feature_path))
    simulation_inputs[model_name] = {
        "model_factory": model_factory,
        "features": features,
        "parameters": subject_parameters,
        "trial_mask": selected_trials,
        "configuration": configuration,
    }




16 — Generate or reuse matching responses and save them
simulations = {}
for model_name, prepared in simulation_inputs.items():
    model_factory = prepared["model_factory"]
    features = prepared["features"]
    subject_parameters = prepared["parameters"]
    selected_trials = prepared["trial_mask"]
    configuration = prepared["configuration"]
    simulation_path = simulation_paths[model_name]
    metadata_path = simulation_path.with_suffix(".json")
    saved_metadata = (
        json.loads(metadata_path.read_text()) if metadata_path.exists() else {}
    )
    reuse_responses = (
        not redo_sims
        and model_name not in fitted_now
        and simulation_path.exists()
        and metadata_path.exists()
        and simulation_metadata_matches(saved_metadata, configuration)
    )
    if reuse_responses:
        simulated = load_data(str(simulation_path))
        print("Loaded matching responses:", simulation_path)
    else:
        simulated = simulate_h5_from_h5(
            model_factory,
            data,
            features,
            subject_parameters,
            selected_trials,
            experiment_count=experiment_count,
            rng=jax.random.PRNGKey(simulation_seed),
            simulate_trial_fn=import_from_string(configuration["simulation_function"]),
        )
        simulation_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        save_dict_to_hdf5(simulated, str(simulation_path))
        metadata_path.write_text(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    **configuration,
                    "jaxcmr_version": jaxcmr.__version__,
                    "jax_version": jax.__version__,
                },
                indent=2,
            )
            + "\n"
        )
        print("Saved responses:", simulation_path)
    if filter_repeated_recalls:
        simulated = dict(simulated)
        simulated["recalls"] = repetition.filter_repeated_recalls(simulated["recalls"])
    simulations[model_name] = simulated
print(
    "simulation_paths =",
    {model_name: str(path) for model_name, path in simulation_paths.items()},
)

title: Fitting models
text:
Inspect behavioral predictions
The configured analyses compare observations with saved simulations, using the selected observation subset and analysis-specific conditions. A model can improve the fitting objective while missing a behavioral pattern, so inspect measures relevant to your question.
filter_repeated_recalls affects these comparisons, not the original fit. The saved response files retain the simulated responses before this display filter.


17 — Prepare configured model and observation comparisons
comparison_groups = []
if redo_figures and simulations:
    observed = dict(data)
    if filter_repeated_recalls:
        observed["recalls"] = repetition.filter_repeated_recalls(observed["recalls"])
    datasets = [observed, *simulations.values()]
    names = ["Observed", *[display_labels[name] for name in simulations]]
    comparison_groups.append(
        {
            "analyses": comparison_analysis_configs,
            "datasets": datasets,
            "labels": names,
            "base_masks": [comparison_mask, *[None for _ in simulations]],
            "suffix": "",
        }
    )
    for dataset_index, (dataset, label) in enumerate(zip(datasets, names)):
        comparison_groups.append(
            {
                "analyses": single_analysis_configs,
                "datasets": [dataset],
                "labels": [label],
                "base_masks": [comparison_mask if dataset_index == 0 else None],
                "suffix": f"_single_{dataset_index}",
            }
        )




18 — Plot and save the configured benchmarks
for group in comparison_groups:
    panel_data = group["datasets"]
    analysis_configs = group["analyses"]
    curve_labels = group["labels"]
    base_masks = group["base_masks"]
    for figure, figure_suffix in iter_analysis_figures(
        panel_data, analysis_configs, curve_labels,
        base_masks=base_masks, trial_query=analysis_trial_query,
        confidence_level=confidence_level, figure_size=figure_size,
        suffix=group["suffix"],
    ):
        save_figure(
            str(figure_dir), figure_str, suffix=figure_suffix,
            formats=figure_formats, figure=figure,
        )

title: Fitting models
text:

Use the printed fit_paths in the simulation template. If responses were generated, use simulation_paths in analysis templates and model comparison. Keep response JSON sidecars with their HDF5 files. title: Distance-conditional response probability
text:
Use distance-CRP to ask whether successive recalls favor items that are close according to a supplied distance measure. It reads response files and a global item-distance matrix (or item features), compares transitions with available opportunities, and saves binned curves.
The measure need not be semantic, but its meaning and direction must be clear: smaller values should describe closer items. Every dataset in a comparison must use the same item identities and distance scale.
For input conventions, see the data guide.

title: Distance-conditional response probability
text:
Choose shared distance bins
The bin calculation happens once, then every dataset uses the same edges. Recomputing separate bins for each dataset would make equal horizontal positions describe different distance ranges.
Within each participant, actual transitions in each bin are divided by available opportunities in that bin. Inspect sparse or undefined bins before comparing curves. The plotted means and bootstrap intervals summarize participants, not individual transitions.


10 — Calculate common distance bins for all response datasets
if bin_edges is None or (isinstance(bin_edges, str) and bin_edges == "percentile"):
    edges, centers = compute_distance_bins_percentiles(
        distance_matrix, jnp.asarray(bin_percentiles)
    )
elif isinstance(bin_edges, str) and bin_edges == "min_count":
    edges, centers = compute_distance_bins_min_count(
        datasets[bin_source_index],
        distance_matrix,
        min_transitions_per_subject,
        step=bin_step,
        trial_mask=jnp.any(jnp.stack(masks_by_dataset[bin_source_index]), axis=0),
    )
else:
    edges, centers = jnp.asarray(bin_edges), None
print("Shared distance boundaries:", np.asarray(edges))


Shared distance boundaries: [0.45812285 0.57310474 0.6419725 ]




11 — Prepare the condition and dataset comparison panels
panels = comparison_panels(
    datasets, masks_by_dataset, input_labels, condition_labels,
    mode="conditions" if data_path is not None else "datasets",
    selection_label=selection_label,
)




12 — Calculate, plot and save the selected comparison
fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(panels), 1, figsize=(8, 3.8 * len(panels)), squeeze=False)
for ax, panel in zip(axes.ravel(), panels):
    panel_data = panel["datasets"]
    panel_masks = panel["trial_masks"]
    curve_labels = panel["labels"]
    title = panel["title"]
    plot_dist_crp(
        panel_data,
        panel_masks,
        distance_matrix=distance_matrix,
        bin_edges=edges,
        bin_centers=centers,
        labels=curve_labels,
        contrast_name=contrast_name,
        color_cycle=color_cycle,
        confidence_level=confidence_level,
        axis=ax,
    )
    ax.set_xlabel("Semantic distance (smaller = more similar)")
    ax.set_title(title)

    if ax.get_legend_handles_labels()[1]:
        ax.legend(title=contrast_name)
    if ylim is not None:
        ax.set_ylim(ylim)
    if yticks is not None:
        ax.set_yticks(yticks)
save_figure(str(figure_dir), figure_str)

text:

Check the category lookup
The following cells collect categories from valid positions in the selected lists and check consistency by global item ID. If an external lookup is supplied, its rows must describe the same identities. An item’s category cannot change across the selected observations under this lookup model.


7 — Load optional item-category features
category_features = np.load(resolve_project_path(category_features_path, root_path)) if category_features_path else None
if category_features is not None and category_features.ndim == 2:
    category_features = category_features[:, feature_column]




8 — Collect categories for selected valid study items
ids_blocks, category_blocks = [], []
for dataset, masks in zip(datasets, masks_by_dataset):
    selected = np.logical_or.reduce([np.asarray(mask) for mask in masks])
    ids = np.asarray(dataset["pres_itemids"])[selected].astype(int)
    categories = (
        category_features[np.maximum(ids - 1, 0)]
        if category_features is not None
        else np.asarray(dataset[category_field])[selected]
    )
    if categories.shape != ids.shape or not np.isfinite(categories[ids > 0]).all():
        raise ValueError("Supply one finite category per valid study item.")
    ids_blocks.append(ids[ids > 0])
    category_blocks.append(categories[ids > 0])




9 — Build a consistent item-category lookup
ids = np.concatenate(ids_blocks)
categories = np.concatenate(category_blocks)
category_values = np.unique(categories)
category_by_item = np.full(int(ids.max()), np.nan)
for item_id in np.unique(ids):
    values = np.unique(categories[ids == item_id])
    if len(values) != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Item {item_id} has conflicting categories across the selected inputs."

    category_by_item[item_id - 1] = np.searchsorted(category_values, values[0])

In this notebook, trial_labels can override labels as the condition-label list; trial_query still takes precedence. Keep valid_field aligned with the stored study positions when replacing the example data.

root_path = resolve_project_root(project_root)

title: Data Simulation
text: Simulation has two interfaces: a trial procedure advances a model and generates item codes; the dataset wrapper assigns parameters, repeats trials and returns a RecallDataset. Understanding that boundary makes it possible to supply a different trial procedure while retaining dataset handling.

title: Data Simulation
section: The trial procedure is an entry point
text:
The trial procedure is an entry point
Declaration from jaxcmr.typing:
class TrialSimulator(Protocol):
    def __call__(
        self,
        model: MemorySearch,
        present: Integer[Array, " study_events"],
        trial: Integer[Array, " recalls"],
        rng: PRNGKeyArray,
    ) -> tuple[MemorySearch, Integer[Array, " recall_events"]]: ...
The callback receives a fresh model, its study sequence, a recall sequence and a JAX random key. It returns the updated model and generated within-list item codes. present and trial use the same item coding at this boundary; the dataset adapter translates recorded study positions beforehand.
A compatible function is supplied through simulate_trial_fn to MemorySearchSimulator or simulate_h5_from_h5(). It must preserve the required array shapes and work with the JAX transformations used to run multiple trials. Its use of the supplied recall sequence determines whether the simulation conditions on observed behavior.







Existing trial procedure
Use of the recorded sequence




simulate_study_and_free_recall
Generates recall using the model’s stopping policy, up to the study-width output limit.


simulate_study_first_recall_and_free_recall
Supplies the recorded first recall, then simulates subsequent responses.


simulate_study_free_recall_and_forced_stop
Masks generated responses using the observed nonzero response slots.



The forced-stop procedure, paired with a no-stop model, conditions on the recorded recall length. A matching recall count is imposed, not predicted. Its returned model has processed the sampled sequence before output masking; masking the returned array is not itself a model state update.

title: Data Simulation
text:
The dataset wrapper
simulate_h5_from_h5() accepts and returns in-memory dictionaries despite its name. HDF5 storage is a separate step. Its central arguments are:







Argument
Meaning




model_factory_cls, dataset, features
Model construction and experimental inputs.


parameters
One-dimensional parameter arrays aligned with a subject ID array.


trial_mask
Selected rows of the observation dataset.


experiment_count
Replications of each selected trial.


rng
JAX random key split across generated trials.


simulate_trial_fn
The compatible trial callback above.



Participant IDs need not be consecutive or equal row indices. The wrapper matches each trial’s ID to parameters['subject'], then uses the same entry from every parameter array. Missing IDs, duplicate assignments and unequal column lengths raise an error before responses are generated. Use parameters_for_subjects to broadcast a pooled fit explicitly.
The legacy mapping without subject treats dataset IDs as zero-based row indices into every parameter column. Simulation does not interpret a short column as a pooled fit.


0 — Locate the project inputs
from pathlib import Path

from jaxcmr.helpers import find_project_root, resolve_project_path

try:
    root_path = Path(find_project_root())
except FileNotFoundError:
    root_path = Path.cwd()




Assign pooled parameters to two participants and supply the trial callback
from pathlib import Path
import json
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jaxcmr.helpers import load_data, generate_trial_mask
from jaxcmr.components import context, linear_memory
from jaxcmr.components.termination import NoStopTermination
from jaxcmr.models.cmr import make_factory

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
data = load_data(resolve_project_path("data/Dupertuys2026.h5", root_path))
record = json.loads(Path(resolve_project_path("data/fits/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo.json", root_path)).read_text())
parameters = {name: values[0] for name, values in record["fits"].items()
              if name != "subject"}
for name in ("allow_repeated_recalls", "learn_after_context_update"):
    parameters[name] = bool(parameters[name])

CMRFactory = make_factory(
    mfc_create_fn=linear_memory.init_mfc,
    mcf_create_fn=linear_memory.init_mcf,
    context_create_fn=context.init,
    termination_policy_create_fn=NoStopTermination,
)

from jax import random
from jaxcmr.simulation import (
    simulate_h5_from_h5, simulate_study_free_recall_and_forced_stop,
)

mixed = generate_trial_mask(data, "data['list_type'] == 1")
participant_ids = jnp.unique(data["subject"][mixed])[:2]
trial_mask = mixed & jnp.isin(data["subject"].ravel(), participant_ids)
simulation_parameters = {
    name: jnp.full(participant_ids.size, value)
    for name, value in parameters.items()
}
simulation_parameters["subject"] = participant_ids

simulated = simulate_h5_from_h5(
    model_factory_cls=CMRFactory, dataset=data, features=None,
    parameters=simulation_parameters, trial_mask=trial_mask,
    experiment_count=2, rng=random.PRNGKey(0),
    simulate_trial_fn=simulate_study_free_recall_and_forced_stop,
)
print("Parameter-row IDs:", simulation_parameters["subject"])
print("Selected trials:", int(trial_mask.sum()))
print("Generated participant IDs:", simulated["subject"].ravel())
print("Generated recall shape:", simulated["recalls"].shape)


Parameter-row IDs: [1 2]
Selected trials: 4
Generated participant IDs: [1 1 1 1 2 2 2 2]
Generated recall shape: (8, 12)


This illustration limits the mixed-list selection to two participants and creates two replications per list. Replicating their trials does not create additional participants. Reusing a key with the same computation reproduces its draws; different simulation runs should record their seeds and settings.

title: Data Simulation
text:
The returned dataset
The wrapper repeats study information and trial conditions with each list. It converts generated item codes back to study-position recall codes, using the first occurrence when a study item repeats. The returned dictionary can therefore enter dataset-based recall analyses.


Inspect the dataset boundary after simulation
print("First two generated recall sequences:")
print(simulated["recalls"][:2])
print("Presentations retained:", bool(jnp.array_equal(
    simulated["pres_itemnos"],
    jnp.repeat(data["pres_itemnos"][trial_mask], 2, axis=0),
)))
print("Omitted response fields:", sorted(set(data) - set(simulated)))


First two generated recall sequences:
[[10  5  8 11  4  2  0  0  0  0  0  0]
 [ 3  1  2  8  7 10  0  0  0  0  0  0]]
Presentations retained: True
Omitted response fields: ['rec_itemids']


Original response measurements cannot describe new responses. The wrapper omits rec_itemids, irt, cue_clips and _should_tabulate when present. Supply additional response-dependent field names through recall_dependent_fields. Study-aligned fields remain attached to their lists.
Use Data for coding and storage conventions. The simulation template handles a complete run, saved outputs and behavioral comparisons; the parameter exploration template repeats that procedure under deliberately changed parameters.

title: Data Simulation
section: Checking whether saved responses match a run
text:
Checking whether saved responses match a run
simulation_metadata_matches compares in-memory metadata before your script decides whether to reuse responses:
from jaxcmr.provenance import simulation_metadata_matches

reuse = (
    not force_regeneration
    and not fitted_now
    and simulation_metadata_matches(saved_metadata, expected_configuration)
)
The comparison includes every supplied expected setting; extra saved fields are allowed. Older metadata with jaxcmr_version and jax_enable_x64 inside implementation are accepted when those values are absent at the top level. The function returns a boolean without modifying either mapping. It does not inspect response files, parse JSON, load data, or decide whether a refit permits reuse. Your script still checks file existence, reads metadata and chooses between loading and generating responses. Malformed saved JSON remains a reading error rather than being silently treated as a cache miss. The fitting template always regenerates responses after a new fit. Changes to data or code in place require explicit regeneration: recorded paths and versions do not establish that file contents or calculations are unchanged.

title: Loss Functions
text: A loss turns predictions and observations into an objective for parameter search. Fitters consume the LossFn interface, so the same fitting procedure can use sequence likelihood or a discrepancy between behavioral summaries.

title: Loss Functions
text:
The loss interface
Declaration from jaxcmr.typing:
class LossFn(Protocol):
    def __init__(
        self,
        model_factory_cls: type[MemorySearchModelFactory],
        dataset: RecallDataset,
        features: Float[Array, " word_pool_items features_count"] | None,
    ) -> None: ...

    def __call__(
        self,
        trial_indices: Integer[Array, " trials"],
        base_params: Mapping[str, Float_],
        free_param_names: Iterable[str],
        x: Float[Array, " parameters n_samples"],
    ) -> Float[Array, " n_samples"]: ...
The constructor binds the dataset, optional features and model factory. A compatible loss class is supplied to a fitter as loss_fn_cls; the fitter constructs its callable instance.







Call argument
Responsibility




trial_indices
Explicit dataset row indices to score, rather than a Boolean mask.


base_params
Fixed values and defaults. Free values override matching entries.


free_param_names
Names in the order of the candidate matrix’s parameter axis.


x
Physical model parameters shaped (parameters, candidates). Each column is one candidate.



The result has one objective per candidate. Fitters minimize these values. A custom loss must preserve this argument order, parameter mapping and output shape and support the JAX operations used by its chosen fitter. Search-coordinate transformations belong to the fitting adapter; the loss receives model parameter values.

title: Loss Functions
text:
Likelihood and event masks
Sequence likelihood follows the observed response history, obtains the probability of each event and sums its negative log probability. A LikelihoodMaskFn chooses which events contribute to that sum.
Declaration from jaxcmr.typing:
class LikelihoodMaskFn(Protocol):
    def __call__(
        self, recalls: Integer[Array, " recall_events"]
    ) -> Bool[Array, " recall_events"]: ...
In jaxcmr.loss.transform_sequence_likelihood, MemorySearchLikelihoodLoss accepts this callback as mask_likelihoods. It translates recorded study positions to within-list item codes before calling the mask. The existing mask_trailing_terminations() returns recalls != 0.
The convenient ExcludeTerminationLikelihoodLoss binds that mask and provides the standard three-argument LossFn constructor used by fitters. With the no-stop model used here, the objective scores the recorded item sequence without scoring its length. Zero-coded slots do not contribute. An excluded event does not erase the preceding history that conditions later predictions. A first-recall mask, for example, removes that event’s score while later events still follow it.
